newsitem.title: USA: Cisco to acquire Granite in $220 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Cisco to acquire Granite in $220 mln deal.

text.p: Cisco Systems Inc, the giant computer networking equipment maker, said Tuesday it has reached a definitive agreement to acquire Granite Systems Inc in a stock swap valued at $220 million.
Privately-held Granite was formed in 1995 to design and develop network switching technologies that can move data as fast as one billion bits per second.
In a statement, Cisco said it acquired the company in order to give its customers a greater choice of network technologies.
Cisco's stock was off 1-5/8 to 51-1/8 in early trading.

Under terms of the deal, Cisco would swap $220 million of its common stock for all the outstanding shares and options of Granite. The transaction would be accounted for as a pooling of interests, and it is expected to close by October 1996.

Founded by Andy Bechtolsheim, also a founder of Sun Microsystems Inc, and David Cheriton, professor of computer science at Stanford University, Granite Systems develops high-performance multilayer switching products.
Two of Granites primary areas of focus are gigabit ethernet switching, which can move data at one billion bits per second, and multilayer switching.
Granite's roughly 50 employees, headed by Bechtolsheim, will become part of Cisco Systems' Workgroup Business Unit.
